Substitution of this value into Equation 23.53 yields the appropriate selection intensity, which is corrected for both finite population size and correlation between lines.

When there is a fixed total number of lines to examine, there is a tradeoff between selection intensity and accuracy. The optimal design for known (or estimated) genetic variances can be obtained by numerically evaluating different combinations of the $ n_{2}/n_{3} $ ratio (for fixed values of N) in Equation 23.45 (and its associated components, Equations 23.49 and 23.51–23.53). Weber (1982, 1984; Wricke and Weber 1986) examines index selection under selfing, including both optimal design (in the absence of dominance) and its extension to additional generations of selfing.
